Subject: Private stack connectivity for EdgeWave pilot

Hi Vivek / Redwood team,

Thanks again for walking us through the Private deployment option yesterday. Our infra team asked for a concise comparison of the connectivity approaches so we can confirm whether to proceed with a direct peering-style model, endpoint isolation (PrivateLink-like), or an encrypted site-to-site tunnel for the pilot. Key constraints: we need control-plane isolation, predictable latency for short inference calls (~30-60ms target), and a procurement window that favors minimal new cross-org networking.

Could you share a short decision memo that highlights operational tradeoffs, security implications, and a rough 3-year cost delta? Also -- any preferences you have from other similar customers would be useful.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Private stack connectivity for EdgeWave pilot

Anu — thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together a short note and a sketch of the three patterns. High level first:

- VPC Peering (direct CIDR-level peering) — lowest operational latency, simplest for high-throughput internal traffic, but limited to same-cloud tenancy and scales poorly across lots of accounts. Peering is "flat" networking which can increase blast radius if misconfigured.

- Endpoint isolation (private endpoint / PrivateLink style) — exposes specific service endpoints over managed endpoints. Good for minimizing attack surface and for multi-account access; predictable access patterns and no broad routing changes. Slightly higher per-request overhead but easier for least-privilege networking.

- Site-to-site VPN (encrypted tunnels) — flexible across on-prem and multi-cloud; easy for customers who cannot use provider-native linking. Easier procurement-wise (IPSec appliances / managed gateway) but adds latency/jitter and sizing complexity; can be a maintenance burden long-term.

I attached a diagram (redwood-privatelink-vs-peering-diagram.png) and a simple 3-year cost model (cost-model-3yr.xlsx). Ben / Marissa — can you add a quick note on operational runbook differences and our recommended default for an early pilot?

Next steps: we can recommend a pilot configuration and a short SOW. I’ll draft that once we align on the approach.

Best,

Subject: Re: Private stack connectivity for EdgeWave pilot

+1 on Vivek's framing. Quick operational bullets from the SRE side:

- Peering: Fast path for KV cache hits and streaming; fewer protocol translations. Operationally we need cross-account route validation and a strict IAM/network review. Scaling to many customer VPCs becomes complex (N^2 peering).

- Private endpoints: Easier to audit per-endpoint traffic, supports granular ALB/NLB fronting, and fits well with our prefix/KV caching model. Slightly more work to expose multiple endpoints (control plane, metrics ingest, inference endpoints) but gives tighter ACLs.

- VPN: Good stop-gap for compliance-constrained customers. If latency is critical, we'd recommend dedicated circuits (Direct Connect / Interconnect) instead of generic VPN. For pilot, temporary s2s VPN is acceptable, but transition costs can be significant.

If EdgeWave wants the lowest touch and fastest time-to-demo, my recommendation is: start with endpoint isolation for control-plane + peering for dataplane (if both sides are in same cloud and acceptable to security). That gives the best balance: isolated management surfaces and fast inference egress.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

> +1 on Vivek's framing. Quick operational bullets from the SRE side:

> - Peering: Fast path ...

Adding a short decision checklist so we can capture EdgeWave constraints and pick the right pattern for the pilot:

1) Regulatory / compliance: if EdgeWave requires customer-owned control plane separation or specific CIDR blocking, PrivateLink-style endpoints are easier to certify.
2) Expected concurrency & throughput: peering wins when sustained request rate is large and predictable. For bursty workloads, our batching can smooth but dataplane cost matters.
3) Multi-account/multi-VPC topology: if EdgeWave already uses multiple AWS accounts, endpoints avoid heavy peering fabric.
4) Procurement / time-to-live: VPNs are fastest to stand up (managed tunnel) but carry ops debt.
5) Observability needs: endpoints allow request-level tracing and token-level cost breakdowns without exposing the whole VPC.

Recommendation for pilot (assumes EdgeWave is AWS-first):
- Control plane & metrics: Private endpoints (least privilege, auditable).
- Inference dataplane: If EdgeWave agrees to share VPC peering and both sides are in the same region/account boundary we recommend peering for latency. Otherwise, use an encrypted VPN + health-checking and plan a migration to peering when performance requirements tighten.

I attached a draft SOW skeleton (sow-draft-edgewave.docx) that splits implementation into discovery, pilot, and handover phases with acceptance criteria keyed to latency and request success rate.

Subject: Re: Private stack connectivity for EdgeWave pilot — decision log

Anu / EdgeWave team — thanks for the quick responses and detail. Summarizing the decision log and next steps below so we have a single source of truth:

Decision summary (pilot):
- Control plane: Private endpoint (endpoint-isolation pattern). Rationale: least privilege, auditability, and simpler compliance sign-off.
- Dataplane (inference traffic): Start with VPC peering for the pilot if EdgeWave can accept cross-account peering (same cloud/region). If not feasible, deploy a temporary site-to-site encrypted VPN and schedule migration to peering after pilot acceptance. Rationale: peering gives best latency for short inference calls; VPN is fallback to avoid blocking the pilot.

Acceptance criteria (pilot):
- 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency <= 80ms for standard 512-token prompts during pilot test window.
- Error rate < 1% for production-like traffic replay.
- Auditable control-plane logs forwarded to EdgeWave SIEM (via private endpoint).

Action items / owners:
- EdgeWave: confirm whether they can approve cross-account peering (Anu) — due 2027-05-06.
- Redwood (Marissa): stand up private endpoints for control-plane + attach RBAC and log-forwarding config — ETA 2027-05-10.
- Redwood (Ben): if peering approved, coordinate route and ACL validation, run perf smoke tests — ETA 2027-05-12. If peering denied, coordinate temporary VPN build and test.
- Vivek: finalize SOW and send draft DocuSign link; attach cost run and diagrams.

I attached the SOW draft, the cost model, and the diagram. HubSpot: HS|EW-3472 has been updated with the decision.

If everyone is aligned I’ll send the SOW and initial onboarding ticket.
